messages:
alice: Heads-up: after landing the kernel selector change yesterday, we started seeing sporadic NaNs in attention for long-context GPT-style runs (seq_len 8k+). Repro attached in logs below.
ben: ugh. can you paste the failing stack/log snippet?
alice: paste: 
```
> runtime: selected kernel posenc_rotary_v2_bf16
> step 1243: forward_attention -> runtime/kernel_posenc.cu:457
> CUDA kernel launched, then NaN detected in kv-cache accumulation
> traceback: kv_accumulate -> posenc_apply -> qk_attention
> tensor stats: attn_weights mean=NaN, max=NaN
```
cheng: thanks. quick theory: the rotary multiplier path that switched to fused complex MUL+scale under bf16 can overflow when rotation angles are large and we do in-place accumulation. the new kernel removed an eps clamp we had in the old scalar path.
emily: does this only repro on bf16 or also fp16?
alice: so far only bf16 on A100s and some older GPUs. fp16 seems OK but slower to repro.
derek: what's the perf delta if we reintroduce the clamp? any microbench?
ben: a small clamp (like scale = exp(clamp(log_scale, -20, 20))) costs almost nothing in CUDA math ops. main worry is branch divergence.
cheng: prototype patch: add a numeric guard in posenc kernel: after rotation mul, do `if (!isfinite(v)) v = v * safe_scale` and clamp exp range. also consider doing accumulation in fp32 for the accum buffer only.
emily: could we use mixed path: for seq < 1024 keep fast fused path, for > 1024 use safe accumulation (fp32 or clamp)? that keeps perf for 99% of calls.
alice: that sounds good. I can add a runtime flag `posenc_numeric_mode` with values `fast` and `safe` and let kernel selector pick it based on seq_len and model config.
ben: add an env override too so we can force safe in Dedicated customers who hit this.
cheng: implementation note: avoid extra copies—do accumulation into an fp32 temp register rather than separate buffer if possible. that keeps memory traffic minimal.
derek: estimate perf hit: safe path ~ +8-12% latency at seq 8k on our microbench. still acceptable vs OOM/NaNs.
infra-bot: ci/presubmit: posenc_unit_tests failed on linux-gpu-rt-3 (flaky numeric). See: https://ci.redwood/1234
ci-bot: created jira-4567 "posenc: add safe numeric mode and backstop clamp" and assigned to @alice and @cheng
emily: for rollout plan: patch -> canary on hosted with safe mode enabled for seq_len > 4k -> monitor token-level NaN/regression -> flip selector default after 48h green.
alice: working on PR now. will include repro harness and perf numbers. tagging @derek for perf review. :thumbsup:
ben: thanks. if we see any customer-timers spike we can push runtime feature flag to Dedicated control plane as a hotfix.
cheng: one more thought: ALiBi variants need different angle scaling; ensure clamp thresholds are parameterized per posenc type.
alice: noted. will add per-posenc config in kernel registry.
emily: nice work team — small change but big safety win. :raised_hands:
